issues.where: Lessons 3 and 4/5 (lesson sequence): ribosomes and membrane-bound organelles
issues.problem: Lesson 3 says both cell types have ribosomes that are 'not membrane-bound'. Lessons 4 and 5 list ribosomes among the organelles. Lesson 7 says cheek cells show only membrane, cytoplasm and nucleus. Lesson 3 also says the nucleus 'allows... gene expression to be regulated', which is not the same as saying the nucleus protects DNA. These are minor and do not contradict each other directly.

Section 2(a) asks what animal cells have that plant cells lack and gives lysosomes and centrioles. This is consistent with Lesson 5. However, the exemplar in (b) says cheek cells lack a large central vacuole. Both claims match the lessons, so there is no conflict here.

The prompt asks for the 'cell organisation hierarchy' and the exemplar adds fibroblasts forming connective tissue in the dermis. Lesson 10 taught only epithelial tissue, skin, the integumentary system and the body. Connective tissue and the dermis were never taught, so the exemplar uses content from outside the lessons.

The prompt's example of a root hair cell and a palisade cell in the same bean plant says the root hair cell has no chloroplasts while palisade cells are packed with them. Lesson 9 did not teach that root hair cells lack chloroplasts. The prompt also hands students the neutrophil and fibroblast examples, so the answer to (b) is given away.
